newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dollar seen rangebound before next leg up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dollar seen rangebound before next leg up.

text.p: The outlook for the dollar remains bullish but trading might be confined within 1.7330 to 1.7225 mark and 116.85 to 115.70 yen ranges for the rest of the day, analysts said.

"Essentially, we'll see a range-bound session," said Ben Morden, a technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc. "Given all the volatility lately, to see North American price action drift today is probably just a normal reaction in the market place."
Key support for the day in dollar/mark lies near the Tuesday low at 1.7223.
So long as that prop remains intact, the greenback is expected to make another stab at the cycle high from April 28 at 1.7389 marks, chartists said.
"While we're above (1.7225 marks), I'm looking for 1.7380/90 and potentially 1.7490 marks," said Thom Worden, global technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Worden said a strong dollar/Swiss could pave the way higher for dollar/mark and dollar/yen.
"Dollar/Swiss is just going through the roof here. So I'm looking for a move up in dollar/Swiss to 1.4470 or so," Worden said.
Analysts also said a steadier mark/yen might, in the short-term, allow dollar/yen to levitate towards initial resistance in the mid 116s.

"I'm probably focused more to the upside now, slightly. I wouldn't say back up to 116.85 but maybe back up to 116.35/50 yen, because mark/yen's break down ... might be done for the day and that was the drag on dollar/yen (down to the early low at 115.70)," Morden said.
Mark/yen is found support near 67.00, where profit-taking was recorded, Morden said.
If dollar/yen stages a breakout above 116.80/90, it should make a dash for 118 or even 118.50, analysts said.
Key support is still located near last week's lows in the 115.10 to 115.25 yen area, they said.
At 1135 EDT/1535 GMT on Tuesday, the dollar was trading around 116.03/13 yen, up from 115.87/97 yen at the open and at 1.7260/70 marks, up from 1.7258/63.
